trend.title: Texas commercial loans flagged for October foreclosure auctions top $1 billion, up from under $800 million in September
trend.scope: Texas commercial properties posted for October 2026 foreclosure sales (Roddy's Foreclosure Listing Service data, reported by The Real Deal)
trend.metric: More than $1 billion in loans flagged for October auctions vs. under $800 million in September; 46 properties, 18 loans rolled over from earlier postings
trend.summary: Commercial loans posted for Texas foreclosure sales in October exceed $1 billion in value, a sharp rebound from a September total below $800 million, according to Roddy's Foreclosure Listing Service data. The October list covers 46 properties, with Bexar County accounting for 13 of them, more than any other county in the count. Eighteen of the loans had been posted for foreclosure before and carried over into October, a sign of drawn-out lender negotiations or ongoing litigation. The largest new postings include a $98 million loan on a Downtown Dallas office tower and a $94 million loan on a Houston apartment complex.
trend.significance: Texas nonjudicial foreclosure lets lenders post and sell commercial collateral within weeks, so a rising posting total is an early read on distress that will show up as workout negotiations, temporary restraining order fights and lender-liability suits before any sale. Repeat postings in particular mark borrowers using the threat of auction to force modifications, and the mix of office, multifamily and hotel collateral shows the pressure is not confined to one property type.
